newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARIAN MAIZE, WHEAT FUTURES CONTINUE TO RISE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARIAN MAIZE, WHEAT FUTURES CONTINUE TO RISE.

text.p: Speculative purchases on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) continued to drive up wheat and maize futures prices on Thursday.

Both have has been firming for the last three weeks following a slump in prices as the market became aware of hundreds of thousands of surplus wheat and maize stocks for which the players did not see buyers, traders said.
They said prices on the physical markets were higher than in futures deals, but the rising trend on the BCE was unjustified by market fundamentals.

"Prices should go down, but one or two brokerages are buying milling wheat aggressively and the smaller ones are following," said Swap Ugynoki Kft's Imre Uzonyi. "A collapse is certain to come, and whoever closes positions quickly will take profits."
Almost all milling wheat and feed wheat maturities traded on Thursday rose by the daily limit of 400 forints per tonne while maize futures firmed by 200 to 350 forints.
The most actively traded milling wheat maturity, August, finished up by 400 forints at 21,240, in 206 lots, while May wheat rose 400 forints in 180 lots, to end at 25,100 forints.
July maize closed at 18,000 forints, up 400, with a total volume of 250 lots.

Traders said they did not a see real chance for the sale of surplus wheat and maize stocks, as Bulgarian buying interest was not promising due to the uncertain solvency of buyers in the southern European country, while Serb purchases were likely to be limited to small amounts.
